question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)+y(t)-5 \\ {y}^{′}(t)={y}^{2}(t)+x(t)-3\end{aligned}
$$

Given the system of differential equations, select the correct options below.

The Jacobian determinant of the system at the equilibrium point ${x}^{∗}=[2,\text{ }1]^{T}$ is given as

$$
J(2,1)={{field-1}}.
$$

At this point, the system is 
{{field-2}}
at ${x}^{∗}.$
question.worked_solution:
The system can be rewritten in matrix form as 

$$
{x}^{′}=\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and 
$\text{\boldsymbol}f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+y-5 \\ {y}^{2}+x-3\end{aligned}].$

We need to compute the Jacobian determinant of $\text{\boldsymbol}f(x).$ 

In our case, we have the following:

$$
J=|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}|
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+y-5)=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+y-5)=1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2}+x-3)=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}+x-3)=2y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
J=|\begin{aligned}2x & 1 \\ 1 & 2y\end{aligned}|.
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}J(2,1) & =|\begin{aligned}2(2) & 1 \\ 1 & 2(1)\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot 2-1\cdot 1 \\  & =7 \\  & \ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the Jacobian determinant is not zero, our system is $\text{almost linear}$ at ${x}^{∗}.$
